nota: Las 88 constelaciones de la UAI: area en grados cuadrados y puesto por tamano (Wikipedia, «IAU designated constellations by solid angle»: la suma es la esfera entera, 41.253), origen (Wikipedia, «IAU designated constellations»: ptolomeo = las 48 del Almagesto, s. II; keyser = Keyser y De Houtman, globo de Plancius de 1598 y Uranometria de Bayer de 1603; plancius; hevelius = Firmamentum Sobiescianum, 1690; lacaille = 1756; argo = las tres de Argo Navis que Lacaille separo; vopel = Coma Berenices, asterismo antiguo, constelacion desde Caspar Vopel, 1536), el significado en ingles y la estrella mas brillante de la misma tabla, la pagina de donde sale la curiosidad de cada una (idiomas/cielo/<idioma>.json, cieloCurCon*): Star Tales de Ian Ridpath (ridpath, por https; Corvus y Crater comparten pagina) y, para Orion, cuya pagina de Star Tales no se dejo leer, el articulo de Wikipedia (wiki); mas, las paginas de Wikipedia de una estrella cuando la UAI le dio nombre despues de escrita la de Star Tales; y cita, lo que dice esa pagina y de donde sale cada frase (antes, el comentario de encima de cada fila; desde que las curiosidades van un fichero por idioma, aqui). Leido todo el 22 de octubre de 2026. Ese mismo dia se volvio a cotejar cada curiosidad con su pagina; 23 paginas de Star Tales (Aur, Boo, CMi, Col, Cyg, Dor, Gem, Her, Hor, Hyi, Leo, Lep, Lyn, Mic, Mus, Pav, Phe, Sco, Tel, Tri, Tuc, Vol y Vul) no se pudieron volver a leer, y en ellas solo cuenta como prueba lo que la cita lleva entre «», copiado en la primera lectura: lo demas se contrasto con Wikipedia en ingles, y se quito o se corrigio lo que no estaba en ninguna de las dos. El modulo lleva una copia sin las citas (CIELO_CONS); tools/auditar_cielo.js (parte 14a) coteja las dos y la suma de las areas.

And.cita: Star Tales, Andromeda: «One of the 48 Greek constellations listed by Ptolemy in the Almagest»; encadenada a una roca por la vanidad de su madre; «At a distance of around 2.5 million light years, the Andromeda Galaxy is the farthest object visible to the naked eye»; Alpheratz, «originally shared with neighbouring Pegasus», «now assigned exclusively to Andromeda», del arabe al-faras, «the horse».

Ant.cita: Star Tales, Antlia: Lacaille, «la Machine Pneumatique», «the single-cylinder type of pump used by the French physicist Denis Papin»; Baily la acorto a Antlia en 1845; «contains no objects of note»; se escribe mal como «Antila».

Aps.cita: Star Tales, Apus: Keyser y De Houtman; ave del paraiso; del griego apous, «footless»; pieles sin patas ni alas, las primeras «brought back to Europe by the survivors of Ferdinand Magellan's round-the-world voyage in 1522»; en el globo de Plancius, «Apis Indica», apis (abeja) por avis (ave); 4.ª magnitud.

Aqr.cita: Star Tales, Aquarius: Ptolomeo; Ganimedes, «Zeus became infatuated with the shepherd boy and swooped down on the Trojan plain in the form of an eagle»; la jarra, «Y-shaped asterism of four stars centred on 4th-magnitude Zeta Aquarii»; el agua acaba en Fomalhaut, «now the exclusive property of the neighbouring Piscis Austrinus».

Aql.cita: Star Tales, Aquila: Ptolomeo; «the eagle was the bird of Zeus, carrying (and retrieving) the thunderbolts»; en una version rapto a Ganimedes; Altair «comes from the Arabic al-nasr al-tā'ir», el aguila que vuela; «The southern part of Aquila was subdivided by Ptolemy into a now-obsolete constellation called Antinous», dibujada en algunos mapas «as a young man being held in the eagle's claws».

Ara.cita: Star Tales, Ara: Ptolomeo; el altar donde los dioses juraron «before their fight against the Titans», «Zeus then placed the altar of the gods in the sky»; «usually depicted with its base to the north and its flames rising southwards»; Ptolomeo conto 7 estrellas, de las 8 de Bayer «the eighth star is entirely spurious».

Ari.cita: Star Tales, Aries: Ptolomeo; el carnero del vellocino de oro: Frixo y Hele, «Helle's grip failed and she fell into the channel between Europe and Asia»; Hamal, del arabe al-hamal, «cordero»; el equinoccio de primavera, «first point of Aries», esta hoy «in the neighbouring constellation Pisces» por la precesion, unos 30°.

Aur.cita: Star Tales, Auriga (auriga.html, leida sin www; la primera version de esta fila salio de Wikipedia y se rehizo con Star Tales): Ptolomeo, «Heniochos»; «The most popular interpretation is that he is Erichthonius, a legendary king of Athens», «He became the first person to harness four horses to a chariot»; «Auriga contains the sixth-brightest star in the sky, known as Capella, a Roman name meaning 'she-goat'», segun Arato la cabra Amaltea «who suckled the infant Zeus»; los cabritillos, «Eta and Zeta Aurigae»; una estrella compartida con Tauro: «the bull has kept the tip of his horn but the luckless charioteer has lost his right foot»; «Of his chariot itself there is no sign»; «There is no legend to explain why the charioteer is so encumbered with livestock».

Boo.cita: Star Tales, Boötes (bootes.html, leida sin www; rehecha con Star Tales, la primera version salio de Wikipedia): Ptolomeo; la Odisea de Homero ya lo nombra; «the constellation represents Arcas, son of the god Zeus»; o Icario: «the god Dionysus taught Icarius how to cultivate vines and make wine»; los pastores «became so intoxicated that their friends thought they had been poisoned, and in revenge they killed Icarius»; «Boötes contains the fourth-brightest star in the entire sky, Arcturus», «Its name means 'bear guard' in Greek»; los perros (Canes Venatici) quiza por una mala traduccion: el arabe del cayado del pastor «was misread by the translator, Gerard of Cremona, as al-kilab, meaning dogs».

Cae.cita: Star Tales, Caelum: Lacaille, «les Burins» (1756), Caelum Scalptorium (1763), Caelum: «In 1844 the English astronomer John Herschel proposed shortening the name to Caelum», «Francis Baily adopted this suggestion in his British Association Catalogue of 1845»; dos buriles cruzados atados con una cinta; «There are no legends associated with the constellation»; «its stars are faint, of 4th magnitude and below»; 81.ª en tamaño.

Cam.cita: Star Tales, Camelopardalis: Plancius, en un globo celeste; «camel leopards», cuello de camello y manchas de leopardo; Jacob Bartsch (1624) la tomo por el camello de Rebeca, explicacion «unsatisfactory»; β (4,0) brilla mas que α (4,3); Hevelius le catalogo 32 estrellas; 18.ª en tamaño.

Cnc.cita: Star Tales, Cancer: Ptolomeo; el cangrejo que mordio a Heracles, «Heracles angrily stamped on the crab, crushing it», Hera lo puso en el cielo; la mas debil del zodiaco, «only six stars brighter than magnitude 5.0»; el Pesebre M44, «a hazy-looking patch which the Greeks called Φάτνη (Phatne), the Manger»; «praesepe can mean both 'manger' and 'hive'».

CVn.cita: Star Tales, Canes Venatici: Hevelius, con estrellas debiles bajo la cola de la Osa Mayor; dos lebreles de Bootes, Asterion («Starry») y Chara («Dear»); Cor Caroli, por Carlos I, «beheaded by parliamentarians in 1649»; la galaxia del Remolino M51, cuya espiral vio lord Rosse en 1845, «around 25 million light years away».

CMa.cita: Star Tales, Canis Major: Ptolomeo, «Kyon»; Lelape, «the dog given by Zeus to Europa», que atrapaba cualquier presa; «Cephalus inherited the dog, and took it with him to Thebes», donde «a vicious fox was ravaging the countryside», «so swift of foot that it was destined never to be caught»; «so Zeus turned them both to stone» y «the dog he placed in the sky as Canis Major, without the fox»; Sirio, «the most brilliant star in the entire night sky», 8,6 años luz, enana blanca que orbita cada 50 años.

CMi.cita: Star Tales, Canis Minor (canisminor.html, leida sin www; rehecha con Star Tales, la primera version salio de Wikipedia): Ptolomeo; «Representing the smaller of the two dogs of Orion»; Mera, el perro de Icario, y su hija Erigone: «Icarius is identified with the constellation Boötes, Erigone is Virgo, and Maera is Canis Minor»; Procion, «meaning 'before the dog' or 'foredog'», «the eighth-brightest star in the heavens, 11.5 light years away», con «a small, hot companion star called a white dwarf that orbits it every 41 years»; «Ptolemy in the Almagest catalogued just two stars in Canis Minor».

Cap.cita: Star Tales, Capricornus: Ptolomeo; Aigokeros, «goat-horned»; de sumerios y babilonios, SUHUR-MASH-HA, «goat-fish»; Pan, que ayudo a los dioses contra los Titanes y aviso de Tifon: «Zeus placed the image of Pan in the sky»; en tiempos griegos el Sol estaba aqui en el solsticio de invierno, hoy «in Sagittarius»; la mas pequeña del zodiaco, menos de un tercio de Virgo.

Car.cita: Star Tales, Carina: Lacaille partio Argo Navis en tres; «usually described as the keel», en realidad «the main body or hull of the ship»; Canopus, «the second-brightest star in the entire sky», gigante blanco cremoso a algo mas de 300 años luz, por el piloto de Menelao, «There Canopus died of a snake bite»; Eta Carinae «brighter than Canopus in 1843». Lo de Tenerife sale del catalogo (datos/cielo.json, latitud 28,3): Canopus culmina a 9° sobre el horizonte sur; la parte 14a lo comprueba.

Cas.cita: Star Tales, Cassiopeia: Ptolomeo; «the vain and boastful wife of King Cepheus of Ethiopia»; «Each night she circles the celestial pole, sometimes upright, sometimes hanging upside down»; la W: Schedar 2,2 y Caph 2,3; la estrella de Tycho, noviembre de 1572, «Supernova 1572 reached magnitude –4, comparable to Venus», visible mas de un año.

Cen.cita: Star Tales, Centaurus: Ptolomeo; Quiron, el centauro sabio, herido por una flecha envenenada de Heracles: inmortal, «Rather than let him suffer endlessly, Zeus agreed» a que cediera su inmortalidad a Prometeo; Alfa Centauri, «4.3 light years away», la tercera mas brillante; Rigil Kentaurus, «centaur's foot»; Omega Centauri, el mayor cumulo globular, para Ptolomeo una estrella de 5.ª magnitud, cumulo desde Halley en 1678. Lo de Tenerife sale del catalogo (latitud 28,3): Rigil Kentaurus culmina a 0,9° y Omega Centauri (C80, NGC 5139) a 14,2°; la parte 14a lo comprueba.

Cep.cita: Star Tales, Cepheus: Ptolomeo; el rey de Etiopia, marido de Casiopea, «instructed by the Oracle of Ammon to chain his daughter Andromeda»; Alderamin, mag. 2,5, en el hombro; Delta Cephei, «a pulsating supergiant that varies in brightness every 5.4 days», prototipo de las cefeidas, «that astronomers use for estimating distances in space».

Cet.significado_en: sea monster (later interpreted as a whale)
Cet.cita: Star Tales, Cetus: Ptolomeo; Ketos, cualquier monstruo marino, en latin «ballena»; el monstruo que Poseidon envio «to ravage the coast of Cepheus's territory», y al que el oraculo mando «to offer up his daughter Andromeda as a sacrifice»; «Perseus drove his diamond-hard sword deep into its right shoulder»; cuarta mas grande; Mira (Omicron Ceti), gigante roja de brillo variable, anotada por David Fabricius en 1596; Menkar, «nostrils», «a misnomer since this star lies on the beast's jaw».

Cha.cita: Star Tales, Chamaeleon: Keyser y De Houtman, 1595-97; «named after the colour-changing lizard»; Lodewyckz: «I saw that they flick their tongues at flies which they thus catch and eat»; en el globo de Hondius de 1600 caza la Mosca vecina; Bayer dibujo la mosca como abeja, «Apis»; 4.ª magnitud; 79.ª.

Cir.cita: Star Tales, Circinus: Lacaille, 1750s; «a pair of dividing compasses as used by geometers, draughtsmen, and navigators»; le Compas (1756), Circinus (1763); «squeezed in their folded position between the forefeet of Centaurus and Triangulum Australe»; «the smallest of Lacaille's 14 inventions, and the fourth-smallest constellation in the entire sky»; «Le Compas du Géomètre».

Col.cita: Star Tales, Columba (columba.html, sin www): Plancius, «first shown as a separate constellation in 1592 on a celestial hemisphere», con estrellas que Ptolomeo «had catalogued as lying outside Canis Major»; «Noah's dove, sent out from the Ark to find dry land», que volvio «with an olive branch in its beak, a sign that the Flood was at last subsiding»; o la paloma de los argonautas «between the sliding doors of the Clashing Rocks»; en China, Shi, «droppings from the celestial toilet Ce in Lepus».

Com.cita: Star Tales, Coma Berenices: Ptolomeo solo anota «a nebulous mass, called the lock»; «first shown as a separate constellation in 1536» (Vopel); «Berenice was a real person who, in 246 BC, married her cousin, Ptolemy III Euergetes»; de la tercera guerra siria, «if he returned victorious she would cut off her hair in gratitude to the gods»; «On Ptolemy's safe return the following year»; «But the following day the tresses were missing»; Conon: «the hair of Berenice had gone to join the constellations»; «the court poet Callimachus»; «now known as the cluster Melotte 111».

CrA.cita: Star Tales, Corona Australis: Ptolomeo; «known to the Greeks not as a crown but as a wreath»; Arato, «a circlet of stars beneath the forefeet of Sagittarius»; «Perhaps it has slipped off the archer's head»; «there seem to be no legends associated with it», salvo que sea la corona que Dionisio puso en el cielo tras sacar a su madre del inframundo; «None of the stars of Corona Australis is brighter than fourth magnitude»; de las 13 de Ptolomeo, una es hoy «Alpha Telescopii»; en China, una tortuga, «Bie».

CrB.cita: Star Tales, Corona Borealis: Ptolomeo; «the golden crown worn by Princess Ariadne of Crete when she married the god Dionysus», hecha por Hefesto «and was studded with jewels from India»; Teseo la abandono en Naxos; Dionisio, tras la boda, «joyfully tossed the crown into the sky where its jewels transformed into stars»; en una version «its sparkling light helped Theseus find his way through the labyrinth»; Alphecca, «once also known as Gemma, the Latin for 'jewel'»; en China, Guansuo, «the prison for working-class miscreants».

Crv.cita: Star Tales, «Corvus and Crater» (corvusandcrater.html; corvus.html no se dejo leer): «Apollo was about to make a sacrifice to Zeus and sent the crow to fetch water from a running spring»; «the crow waited several days for the fruit to ripen» (higos); volvio con una serpiente de agua, «blaming the serpent for blocking the spring»; Apolo «condemned the crow to a life of thirst», «perhaps one explanation for the rasping call of the crow»; en el cielo, «pecking at the water snake's coils»; «The brightest star in Corvus is Gamma Corvi, known as Gienah»; «Alpha is only of magnitude 4.0».

Crt.cita: Star Tales, «Corvus and Crater»: Krater, «a bowl or vase used for mixing wine with water, rather than a cup as we know it»; en el lomo de la Hidra, «shown tilted towards the crow but tantalizingly just out of the thirsty bird's reach»; «In Crater the brightest star is Delta, magnitude 3.6; Alpha is only magnitude 4.1»; «Corvus and Crater are both constellations in which the star labelled Alpha is not the brightest»; («seemingly Ptolemy, or perhaps a later scribe, transposed left and right» es del ala del Cuervo, no de la Copa); en China, Yi, «the wings of the Red Bird».

Cru.cita: Star Tales, Crux: Ptolomeo catalogo sus estrellas como «part of the hind legs of Centaurus»; «subsequently became lost from view to Europeans because of the effect of precession» y «were rediscovered during the 16th century by seafarers venturing south»; «navigators began using the cross as a pointer to the south celestial pole»; «Acrux is the most southerly first-magnitude star»; «The smallest of all the 88 constellations». Lo de Tenerife sale del catalogo (datos/cielo.json, latitud 28,3): γ, β y δ Crucis culminan a 4,6°, 2,0° y 3,0° sobre el horizonte; Acrux, a -1,4°: no sale (la parte 14a lo comprueba).

Cyg.cita: Star Tales, Cygnus (cygnus.html, sin www): Ptolomeo; «the swan is Zeus in disguise, on his way to one of his innumerable love affairs»; «Out of the egg hatched the beautiful Helen, later to become famous as Helen of Troy»; Deneb, «from dhanab, the Arabic word for 'tail'», «a highly luminous supergiant about 1,400 light years away, the most distant of all first-magnitude stars»; Albireo, «a beautiful coloured double star of green and amber»; «the name Albireo, although it looks Arabic, is completely meaningless»; la Cruz del Norte.

Del.cita: Star Tales, Delphinus: Ptolomeo; Poseidon envio mensajeros tras Anfitrite, «including a dolphin, which found her»; «In gratitude, Poseidon placed the image of the dolphin among the stars»; «Two stars in Delphinus bear the peculiar names Sualocin and Rotanev» (catalogo de Palermo, 1814); «Read backwards, these names spell out Nicolaus Venator, the Latinized form of Niccolò Cacciatore (1770-1841)», ayudante de Piazzi; «It is usually said that Cacciatore was responsible for the naming, which would make him the only person to have named a star after himself and got away with it»; «However, it is equally possible that the names were applied by Piazzi to honour his heir apparent, or 'dauphin' (dolphin)».

Dor.cita: Star Tales, Dorado (dorado.html, sin www): Keyser y De Houtman; «the colourful dolphinfish Coryphaena hippurus (also known as mahi-mahi)», «not the goldfish commonly found in ponds and aquaria»; «Dutch explorers observed these large predatory fish chasing flying fish», y en el cielo va tras Volans; «most of the Large Magellanic Cloud», «about 170,000 light years away»; la Tarantula, «bright enough to have been shown as a star on Johann Bayer's southern star chart of 1603»; Xiphias, el pez espada, en Kepler (1627).

Dra.cita: Star Tales, Draco: Ptolomeo; «This dragon, named Ladon, guarded the precious tree on which grew the golden apples»; Ladon «could talk in different voices»; Heracles lo mato «with his poisoned arrows» y Hera lo puso en el cielo; Hercules, con un pie «planted firmly upon its head»; la cola «extends between the two bears»; «Despite its considerable size, the eighth-largest constellation, Draco is not particularly prominent»; «Its brightest star is second-magnitude Gamma Draconis, called Eltanin», «from the Arabic al-tinnin meaning 'the serpent'»; Thuban es la α.

Equ.cita: Star Tales, Equuleus: Ptolomeo, «Hippou Protome, the forepart of a horse»; «the true inventor of Equuleus seems to have been Hipparchus rather than Ptolemy»; «This insignificant constellation, second-smallest in the sky»; «The early mythologists such as Eratosthenes and Hyginus never mentioned this little horse, but perhaps Ptolemy (or Hipparchus) had in mind the story of Hippe»; «Hippe, daughter of Chiron the centaur, one day was seduced by Aeolus»; «When her father came looking for her, Hippe appealed to the gods who changed her into a mare»; «Artemis placed the image of Hippe among the stars, where she still hides from Chiron», «with only her head showing».

Eri.cita: Star Tales, Eridanus: Ptolomeo; «Phaethon, son of the Sun-god Helios, who begged to be allowed to drive his father's chariot across the sky»; «Zeus struck Phaethon down with a thunderbolt»; «With his hair streaming fire, the youth plunged like a shooting star into the Eridanus»; «the sixth-largest in the sky»; Achernar, «from the Arabic akhir al-nahr meaning 'the river's end'»; para Ptolomeo el rio terminaba «17° farther north», en la estrella que Bayer llamo Theta, hoy Acamar; «The present-day Achernar is the only first-magnitude star not listed in Ptolemy's Almagest».

For.cita: Star Tales, Fornax: Lacaille, «depicting a chemist's furnace used for distillation»; le Fourneau (1756), Fornax Chimiae (1763), Fornax (Baily, 1845); «It lies tucked into a bend in the river Eridanus»; «It is sometimes said that Lacaille invented the constellation to honour his countryman Antoine Lavoisier», «a misunderstanding», «since Lavoisier was only 13 years old»; Bode (1801) lo redibujo a partir del «diagram of his experiment to decompose water into its constituents of hydrogen and oxygen» y lo llamo «Apparatus Chemicus», nombre que no cuajo.

Gem.significado_en: twins (Lugal-irra and Meslamta-ea, later Castor and Pollux)
Gem.cita: Star Tales, Gemini (gemini.html, sin www): Ptolomeo; Castor y Polux, los Dioscuros; «Their mother was Leda, Queen of Sparta, whom Zeus visited one day in the form of a swan»; Castor, hijo de Tindareo, mortal; Polux, inmortal; «Castor was run through by a sword thrust from Lynceus»; «Pollux grieved for his fallen brother and asked Zeus that the two should share immortality»; en el cielo, «in close embrace, inseparable to the last»; patronos de los marineros, en el fuego de San Telmo; «Castor is actually a complex system of six stars linked by gravity»; «Although Castor is labelled Alpha Geminorum, it is nearly half a magnitude fainter than Pollux».

Gru.cita: Star Tales, Grus: Keyser y De Houtman; Plancius y Hondius, 1598; Bayer, 1603; «There are no legends associated with Grus, but in Greek mythology the crane was sacred to Hermes»; «Phoenicopterus, the flamingo, first appeared in 1605»; «De Houtman called it Den Reygher, the heron, in his southern star catalogue of 1603»; la γ era para Ptolomeo la punta de la cola del Pez Austral; Alnair, «the bright one from the fish's tail».

Her.cita: Star Tales, Hercules (hercules.htm, sin www): Ptolomeo, «Engonasi», el arrodillado; Arato: «No one knows his name, nor what he labours at»; Eratostenes «identified the figure as Heracles»; «his left foot on the head of the dragon, Draco»; «Hercules wears a lion's skin and in his right hand brandishes a club»; las manzanas de oro y Ladon; «The Nemean lion is identified with the constellation Leo»; «Both the crab (Cancer) and the Hydra are commemorated as constellations»; 5.ª en tamaño.

Hor.cita: Star Tales, Horologium (horologium.html, sin www): Lacaille, «l'Horloge» (1756), Horologium (1763); «a pendulum clock beating seconds, as used for timing his observations»; del tipo «invented by the Dutch scientist Christiaan Huygens in 1656», aunque el suyo «of a much simpler design»; «with a fully marked dial and even a seconds-hand»; Allen (1899), «Horologium Oscillatorium», «but Lacaille never called it that»; Bode lo dibujo con el pendulo de parrilla «invented by the English clockmaker John Harrison in 1726».

Hya.cita: Star Tales, Hydra: Ptolomeo; «Hydra is the largest of the 88 constellations, winding over a quarter of the way around the sky»; «The total length from its westernmost boundary to the easternmost one is 102°.5»; la segunda hazaña de Heracles; vivia en un pantano junto a Lerna, con un aliento «so poisonous that anyone who breathed them died in agony»; «Heracles called for help to his charioteer Iolaus who burned the stump of each head»; «Hydra reputedly had nine heads», «In the sky, though, it is shown with one head only»; «Its only star of note is second-magnitude Alphard», «from the Arabic al-fard appropriately meaning 'the solitary one'».

Hyi.cita: Star Tales, Hydrus (hydrus.html, sin www): Keyser y De Houtman; Plancius, 1598; Bayer, 1603; «Hydrus is a male water snake, whereas the much larger Greek constellation Hydra is a female»; «It represents the sea snakes that the Dutch explorers would have seen on their voyages»; «Hydrus has endured more redesigns than any other constellation»; Bayer la hacia pasar «passing the south celestial pole»; «Lacaille docked the snake's tail to make way for Octans» y la desvio «between the two Magellanic Clouds»; «The brightest stars of Hydrus are of third magnitude, but none have names».

Ind.cita: Star Tales, Indus: Keyser y De Houtman; Plancius, 1598; Bayer, 1603; «The Indian is portrayed brandishing a spear as though hunting»; «he could be a native of the East Indies or southern Africa»; Madagascar, «where the Dutch fleet stayed for several months»; «Or perhaps the figure is symbolic, representing all the indigenous peoples the explorers encountered»; «Bayer's depiction in 1603 showed the Indian face-on with the spear in his left hand»; «On Hevelius's atlas of 1690 the figure is seen from the front and appears to be female»; «Bode has turned him round so he is seen from the back, perhaps to make him right-handed».

Lac.cita: Star Tales, Lacerta: Hevelius (catalogo de 1687, atlas de 1690); «sandwiched between Cygnus and Andromeda like a lizard between rocks»; tambien Stellio, «a type of lizard also known as a starred agama», nombre que cayo en desuso y que la UAI ha dado a α Lacertae; α y β de 4.ª magnitud; las letras griegas son de Baily, 1845; en China, «northern Lacerta was the centre of a spidery shaped figure called Tengshe, the flying serpent», que se metia en las constelaciones vecinas.

Leo.cita: Star Tales, Leo (leo.html, sin www): Ptolomeo; «reputed to be the lion of Nemea, slain by Heracles as the first of his 12 labours»; «Heracles blocked up one of the entrances and went in through the other»; «He grappled with the lion, locking his huge arm around its throat and choking the beast to death»; Regulus, «Latin for 'little king'»; «the Babylonians knew it as LUGAL, 'king'»; «One of the first to adopt it was Copernicus, who is sometimes wrongly said to have invented the name»; «The head and chest are outlined by six stars arranged in the shape of a sickle»; la punta de la cola, «now part of Coma Berenices».

LMi.cita: Star Tales, Leo Minor: Hevelius, «A lion cub accompanying Leo», 18 estrellas debiles; «there are no legends associated with it»; Baily (1845) dio la β y dejo la mas brillante «unlettered by mistake»; 46 LMi, hoy Praecipua; 4.ª magnitud.

Lep.cita: Star Tales, Lepus (lepus.html, sin www): Ptolomeo, Lagoos; «Lepus cowers under the feet of Orion, the hunter»; «Eratosthenes tells us that Hermes placed the hare in the sky because of its swiftness»; «At one time there were no hares on the island of Leros, until one man brought in a pregnant female», «Soon, everyone began to raise hares and before long the island was swarming with them», «They overran the fields and destroyed the crops», «By a concerted effort, the inhabitants drove the hares out of their island», «They put the image of the hare among the stars as a reminder that one can easily end up with too much of a good thing»; Arato: el Perro «pursues the hare in an unending race»; en China, Junjing, «a well of drinking water for the army», y Ce, «a toilet».

Lib.cita: Star Tales, Libra: para Ptolomeo aun «the Claws of Scorpius» (Chelae); la balanza «became established in the first century BC among the Romans»; babilonios, ZIB.BA.AN.NA, «the balance of heaven»; la unica del zodiaco que no es un ser vivo; «the scales of justice held aloft by the goddess» (Virgo/Dike); Zubenelgenubi (2,7) y Zubeneschamali (2,6), «the southern claw» y «the northern claw»; mayor que Escorpio pero mucho menos vistosa.

Lup.cita: Star Tales, Lupus: Ptolomeo; Therion, «an unspecified wild animal», Bestia para los romanos; el lobo «seems to have become established in Renaissance times»; «impaled on a long pole called a thyrsus» que sostiene el Centauro, «holding the animal towards the altar» (Eratostenes); «The fact that it is an imported constellation probably explains why the Greeks had no myths for it»; «None of the stars of Lupus is named»; «its Babylonian identification as UR.IDIM, meaning 'wild dog' or 'wolf'». Wikipedia, «Alpha Lupi» (Star Tales es anterior y dice «None of the stars of Lupus is named»): «The IAU Working Group on Star Names approved the name Uridim for this star on 12 September 2024»; «The Sumerian name for the constellation Lupus was UR.IDIM». La lista de la UAI la da como la mas brillante (datos/constelaciones.json); la parte 14a lo cruza.

Lyn.cita: Star Tales, Lynx (lynx.html, sin www): «Johannes Hevelius, the Polish astronomer who introduced this constellation in his star catalogue of 1687»; quien quisiera verla «would need the eyesight of a lynx»; «It is not known whether Hevelius had in mind the mythological character Lynceus»; «Alpha Lyncis, magnitude 3.1, is the brightest star in the constellation, and the only one with a Greek letter» (Baily, 1845); las entradas 10 y 19 de Flamsteed para la Osa Mayor «are not in the bear at all but in the tail of Lynx»; «some charts of Lynx incorporate a star labelled 10 UMa».

Lyr.cita: Star Tales, Lyra: Ptolomeo; la lira de Orfeo, que Hermes hizo con un caparazon de tortuga y «seven strings matching the seven Pleiades»; Orfeo y Euridice: «must not at any stage look behind him»; Vega, «the fifth- brightest star in the sky», del arabe al-nasr al-waqi', «the swooping eagle or vulture»; Sheliak «harp», Sulafat «the tortoise»; Bode escribia «Wega».

Men.cita: Star Tales, Mensa: Lacaille, la montaña de la Mesa junto a Ciudad del Cabo, «to commemorate Table Mountain near Cape Town, South Africa, from where he catalogued the southern stars in 1751–52»; «Montagne de la Table» (1756), Mons Mensae (1763), Mensa desde Herschel (1844) y Baily (1845); parte de la Gran Nube de Magallanes, «being capped by a white cloud», como el «table-cloth» de la montaña de verdad; «Mensa's brightest stars are of only fifth magnitude».

Mic.cita: Star Tales, Microscopium (microscopium.html, sin www): «Lacaille first showed the constellation on his map of 1756 under the name le Microscope», latinizado en 1763; «an early form of compound microscope, i.e. one that uses more than one lens»; «It incorporates six 'unformed' stars that Ptolemy had listed in his star catalogue as lying outside Piscis Austrinus»; «the constellation's brightest star, Gamma Microscopii of magnitude 4.7»; «The only remarkable thing about Microscopium is that anyone could imagine a separate constellation here».

Mon.cita: Star Tales, Monoceros: Plancius, en un globo, «Monoceros Unicornis»; «was unknown to the ancient Greeks», «fills a large area between Hydra and Orion where there was no Greek constellation»; Bartsch (1624) «pointed to several passages in the Bible that supposedly mention unicorns, although these are now regarded as mistranslations»; la adopto Hevelius en 1690; β mas brillante que α; la nebulosa Roseta, «a wreath-shaped mass of glowing gas with embedded stars»; sin leyendas ni nombres; Gould letreo en 1879.

Mus.cita: Star Tales, Musca (musca.html, sin www): Keyser y De Houtman; Plancius, 1598; De Houtman: «De Vlieghe, Dutch for fly»; Bayer la llamo «Apis, the bee, an alternative title that was widely used for two centuries»; Plancius, «Muia, the Greek for fly»; «the seafarers saw chameleons eating flies during their stopover on Madagascar»; esta junto al Camaleon; «For a time it was known as Musca Australis, when there was also a northern fly, Musca Borealis, in the sky» (que no esta entre las 88 de la UAI).

Nor.cita: Star Tales, Norma: Lacaille, «l'Equerre et la Regle» (1756), Norma (1763), «an architect's set-square and ruler», junto a su Circinus y Triangulum Australe, «a builder's level», «a trio of surveying and drawing instruments»; R. H. Allen la llamo «the Level and Square» por leer mal el mapa frances, «Allen's error has caused confusion ever since»; «The brightest stars of Norma are of only fourth magnitude and none have names»; sus α y β pasaron a Escorpio con los limites nuevos (N y H Sco).

Oct.cita: Star Tales, Octans: Lacaille; el octante de reflexion, inventado en 1730 por John Hadley; «principal instrument des Navigateurs pour observer la hauteur du pole»; abarca el polo sur celeste, «There is, unfortunately, no southern equivalent of the bright northern pole star, Polaris»; ν Octantis 3,7; «The nearest naked-eye star to the south celestial pole is Sigma Octantis», 5,4; α Octantis (5,2) «the faintest star labelled Alpha in any constellation».

Oph.cita: Star Tales, Ophiuchus: Ptolomeo; Ophiouchos, «serpent holder», Asclepio, dios de la medicina, «could also raise the dead»; Zeus lo fulmino con «a thunderbolt» y lo hizo inmortal; Rasalhague, «the head of the serpent bearer»; la estrella de Barnard, 5,9 años luz; la supernova de Kepler, 1604, «the last supernova seen in our Galaxy»; el Sol lo cruza a principios de diciembre, «the 13th sign of the zodiac».

Ori.cita: Orion: la pagina de Star Tales no se dejo leer (robots_disallowed, con y sin www), asi que esta fila sale de Wikipedia, «Orion (constellation)», leida el 22-10-2026: «it was among the 48 constellations listed by the 2nd-century AD astronomer Ptolemy»; «One myth recounts Gaia's rage at Orion, who dared to say that he would kill every animal on Earth. The angry goddess tried to dispatch Orion with a scorpion. This is given as the reason that the constellations of Scorpius and Orion are never in the sky at the same time»; «In ancient Egypt, the stars of Orion were regarded as a god, called Sah», «Sah is syncretized with Osiris»; el Cinturon, «known in Spain and most of Latin America as Las tres Marías»; la nebulosa de Orion, «clearly identified with the naked eye as something other than a star»; «Around 20 October each year, the Orionid meteor shower (Orionids) reaches its peak», «The shower's parent body is Halley's Comet».

Pav.cita: Star Tales, Pavo (pavo.html, sin www): Keyser y De Houtman; Plancius, 1598; Bayer, 1603; Argos, guardian de Io, «ideally suited to the task of watchman, since he had 100 eyes»; Hermes lo durmio y «Hera placed the eyes of Argus on the tail of the peacock»; el pavo, «the sacred bird of Hera», que iba en un carro tirado por pavos; no es el pavo real azul de la India sino «its larger, more colourful, and more aggressive cousin, the Java green peacock»; «The constellation's brightest star, second-magnitude Alpha Pavonis, is called Peacock», nombre puesto «in or around 1937 by the UK's Nautical Almanac Office for use in The Air Almanac, a navigation guide produced for the Royal Air Force».

Peg.cita: Star Tales, Pegasus: Ptolomeo; para los griegos solo Hippos, «the horse», con alas segun Ptolomeo; nacio de Medusa decapitada, «both Pegasus and the warrior Chrysaor sprang from her body»; Belerofonte; «Mount Helicon in Boeotia, home of the Muses», la fuente Hipocrene, «horse's fountain»; Enif, mag. 2,4, del arabe anf, «nose»; 7.ª en tamaño; el Cuadrado de Pegaso, con una esquina que ya es de Andromeda, «allocated exclusively to Andromeda, as Alpha Andromedae»: «now has only three corners».

Per.cita: Star Tales, Perseus: Ptolomeo; el heroe con la cabeza de la Gorgona en la mano izquierda y la espada en la derecha; hijo de Danae, Zeus como «a shower of golden rain»; decapito a Medusa y salvo a Andromeda; Mirfak, «elbow»; Algol, «the demon's head», cada 2,9 dias, «Algol varies in brightness from magnitude 2.1 to 3.4 as the two stars eclipse each other»; Montanari 1671, Goodricke 1783; «a twin cluster of stars now popularly called the Double Cluster» (NGC 869 y 884).

Phe.cita: Star Tales, Phoenix (phoenix.html, sin www): Keyser y De Houtman; Plancius, 1598; Bayer, 1603; «Ovid in his Metamorphoses tells us that the phoenix lived for 500 years»; «A baby phoenix was born from its father's body»; «It is the largest of the 12 figures invented at the end of the 16th century»; «its brightest star, Alpha Phoenicis, known as Ankaa, is of magnitude 2.4»; antes de Keyser y De Houtman, α Phoenicis era la estrella mas brillante de la constelacion china Bakui, una red para cazar pajaros.

Pic.cita: Star Tales, Pictor: Lacaille, «le Chevalet et la Palette», el caballete del pintor con la paleta; «Equuleus Pictorius» (1763); bajo la quilla de Argo, «next to the bright star Canopus»; sus cuatro estrellas mas brillantes las habia catalogado De Houtman como parte de Argo 150 años antes; Pictor desde Herschel (1844) y Baily (1845).

Psc.cita: Star Tales, Pisces: Ptolomeo, Ichthyes; heredada de Babilonia, mitos en el Eufrates; Afrodita y Eros huyen de Tifon y dos peces los salvan (o se vuelven peces): «the Syrians would not eat fish»; Alrescha, mag. 3,8, «the cord», en el nudo; el Circlet; el equinoccio de primavera esta hoy aqui y «precession will carry it into Aquarius around 2597»; «disappointingly faint».

PsA.cita: Star Tales, Piscis Austrinus: Ptolomeo, «the final constellation in Ptolemy's catalogue in the Almagest»; su mitologia «reveals its Babylonian origin»; Derceto «is supposed to have fallen into a lake at Bambyce» y «was saved by a large fish»; por eso (Higino) «the Syrians do not eat fish but they worship the images of fish as gods»; Fomalhaut, «fish's mouth», de primera magnitud; «the fish is shown drinking the water flowing from the jar of Aquarius, a strange thing for a fish to do»; los beduinos veian en Fomalhaut y Achernar «a pair of ostriches».

Pup.cita: Star Tales, Puppis: Lacaille partio Argo Navis en tres (1756, «Pouppe du Navire»); «the poop is separated from the body of the vessel by the rudder»; Canopus, en el timon, cuenta en Carina; «The brightest star in Puppis is in fact second-magnitude Zeta Puppis, called Naos from the Greek word for ship»; «Puppis has no stars labelled Alpha or Beta (and nor does Vela)»; en la Uranographia de Bode (1801), «Partially concealed behind the hind quarters of Canis Major lurks what appears to be a scaly sea creature, identity unknown».

Pyx.cita: Star Tales, Pyxis: Lacaille, «la Boussole» (1756), latinizada en 1763 a «Pixis Nautica (sic)»; la brujula magnetica de los marinos; «Pyxis is an additional constellation invented by Lacaille» (no es una parte de Argo); «the magnetic compass was completely unknown to the ancient Greeks»; sus estrellas α-δ «had been catalogued by Ptolemy as lying in the mast of Argo»; en 1844 John Herschel propuso devolverlas a Argo como Malus, el mastil; lo uso Baily (1845) y Gould volvio a la brujula (1879).

Ret.cita: Star Tales, Reticulum: Lacaille, para recordar la reticula del ocular de su pequeño telescopio en el Cabo (1751-52), «a diamond-shaped aperture cut from a copper plate inserted into the eyepiece»; esta junto a su reloj, Horologium, usado «for timing the passage of stars through the reticle»; antes, el Rhombus de Isaac Habrecht II (globo de 1621); Jamieson (1822) «replaced Reticulum with Solarium, the sundial», «copied by the American Elijah H. Burritt (1794–1838) on his Atlas Designed to Illustrate The Geography of the Heavens of 1835, but was not otherwise widely adopted».

Sge.cita: Star Tales, Sagitta: Ptolomeo; Arato: «alone, without a bow»; «Eratosthenes said it was the projectile with which Apollo killed the Cyclopes»; Higino: «one of the arrows with which Heracles killed the eagle that ate the liver of Prometheus»; Germanico: «the arrow of Eros which kindled in Zeus his passion for the shepherd boy Ganymede»; «the third-smallest constellation in the sky»; «brightest star is actually Gamma Sagittae, magnitude 3.5»; la α (4,4) es Sham, del arabe «arrow».

Sgr.cita: Star Tales, Sagittarius: Ptolomeo; del sumerio «PA.BIL.SAG, a god of war and hunting who they depicted as a centaur-like archer with wings», «adopted by the Greeks, although without the wings»; Eratostenes: no es un centauro (los centauros no usaban arco) sino «Crotus, son of Eupheme, the nurse to the Muses»; «Hyginus in his Fabulae added the information that the father of Crotus was Pan»; «Crotus was said to have invented archery»; «The Muses requested that Zeus place him among the stars»; la Tetera; «Sagittarius A*», el centro de la galaxia; «Alpha Sagittarii is only the 15th brightest star in the constellation».

Sco.cita: Star Tales, Scorpius (scorpius.html, sin www): Ptolomeo; «the Sumerians knew it as GIR-TAB, the scorpion, over 5,000 years ago»; mato a Orion, enviado por Artemis o por la Tierra; «the two constellations are placed opposite each other so that Orion sets as his conqueror the scorpion rises»; Antares, en griego «like Mars» por su color, «a remarkable supergiant star, several hundred times the diameter of our Sun»; «In the first century BC the Romans made the claws into a separate constellation, Libra»; en China, Antares era «Huo, the fire star», el corazon del Dragon Azul.

Scl.cita: Star Tales, Sculptor: Lacaille, «l'Atelier du Sculpteur» (1756), «Apparatus Sculptoris» (1763); «In 1844 the English astronomer John Herschel proposed shortening the name to Sculptor»; «its stars are only of fourth magnitude and fainter; none of them is named»; «Sculptor is the largest of Lacaille's 14 inventions»; Bode (1801) «dispensed with the block of marble and moved the sculptor's tools to the top of the table» y, «In place of the marble block he created the constellation Machina Electrica».

Sct.cita: Star Tales, Scutum: «introduced in 1684 by the Polish astronomer Johannes Hevelius under the title Scutum Sobiescianum»; «He named it in honour of King John III Sobieski of Poland», «who helped Hevelius rebuild his rooftop observatory after a disastrous fire in 1679»; Flamsteed la ignoro (1725, 1729) y Baily la omitio (1845); «the only constellation introduced for political reasons that is still in use»; «Edmond Halley's invention six years earlier of Robur Carolinum, honouring King Charles II of England»; «Robur Carolinum did not survive but Scutum did»; el cumulo del Pato Salvaje, «because its fan-shape resembles a flight of ducks».

Ser.cita: Star Tales, Serpens: Ptolomeo; la serpiente que sujeta Ofiuco (Asclepio); «This constellation is unique, for it is divided into two parts - Serpens Caput, the head, and Serpens Cauda, the tail»; Asclepio «once killed a snake that was miraculously restored to life by a herb placed on it by another snake» y «subsequently used the same technique to revive dead people»; «why he appears to be wrestling with a serpent in the sky is not fully explained»; «Snakes are the symbol of rebirth because they shed their skins every year»; «The most celebrated object in Serpens is a star cluster called M16, embedded in a gas cloud called the Eagle Nebula», con los «pillars of gas» del Hubble.

Sex.cita: Star Tales, Sextans: «introduced by the Polish astronomer Johannes Hevelius in his star catalogue of 1687 under the name Sextans Uraniae»; el sextante con que media las estrellas, «destroyed along with other instruments in a fire at his home in 1679»; «Hevelius had continued to make naked-eye sightings with his sextant throughout his life, even though he used telescopes for observing the Moon and planets»; «it was perhaps to demonstrate the keenness of his eyes that he formed Sextans out of such faint stars»; «The brightest star in the constellation, Alpha Sextantis, is magnitude 4.5»; ninguna tiene nombre; en China, tres eran Tianxiang, «celestial minister».

Tau.cita: Star Tales, Taurus: Ptolomeo; «In the sky, only the front half of the bull is shown»; Zeus «Adopting the shape of a bull» se mezclo con el rebaño, «There was no mistaking who was the most handsome bull»; «Europa ventured to sit on his back» y el se la llevo a nado a Creta; «The bull's eye is marked by the reddish star Aldebaran», que «appears to be a member of the Hyades but is in fact a foreground object 65 light years away», «less than half the distance of the cluster, which lies 150 light years away»; los romanos llamaban a las Hiades «suculae meaning 'piglets'»; las Pleyades, en su lomo.

Tel.cita: Star Tales, Telescopium (telescopium.html, sin www): Lacaille, «le Telescope» (1756), Telescopium (1763); «the type of long, unwieldy refractor suspended from a pole known as an aerial telescope», «as used by J. D. Cassini at Paris Observatory»; tan largos «to reduce chromatic aberration (false colour) produced by the crude lenses of that time»; Baily lo recorto (1845); subia entre Sagitario y Escorpio: «Lacaille's Beta Telescopii, positioned in the pulley at the top of the mast, is now Eta Sagittarii»; la Theta «is humble 45 Ophiuchi»; «Its brightest star, Alpha Telescopii, is magnitude 3.5».

Tri.cita: Star Tales, Triangulum (triangulum.html, sin www): Ptolomeo, Trigonon; Arato y Eratostenes lo llamaban Deltoton, «because its shape resembled a capital delta»; «Eratosthenes said that it represented the Nile river delta»; Higino: «some people also saw it as the island of Sicily» (Trinacria), «the home of Ceres»; «Triangulum contains M33, a galaxy in our Local Group», «visible with binoculars»; «A smaller triangle, Triangulum Minus, was introduced in 1687» por Hevelius, que llamo a este Triangulum Majus; «The constellation's brightest star is actually Beta Trianguli, magnitude 3.0, but this has no name». Wikipedia, «Beta Trianguli» (Star Tales es anterior y dice «this has no name»): «The name Alaybasan was approved for Beta Trianguli A by the IAU Working Group on Star Names on 7 November 2025», un nombre arabe (Al-Aybasan, «the Two Joints»); «it is the brightest star in the constellation Triangulum»; y antes ya se la llamaba Mizan («Mizan has been used as a name for β Trianguli»): por eso «nombre oficial».

TrA.cita: Star Tales, Triangulum Australe: Keyser y De Houtman; el moderno, en el globo de Plancius de 1598 y en Bayer (1603); Lacaille (1756), «le Triangle Austral ou le Niveau», «even showed it with an attached plumb bob, indicating that he regarded it as representing a surveyor's level»; R. H. Allen «transferred the appellation 'level' to the nearby constellation Norma», «thereby confusing generations of astronomers»; «Navigators have named its brightest star Atria, a contraction of its scientific name Alpha Trianguli Australis»; «The three main stars of Triangulum Australe are brighter than those of their northern counterpart».

Tuc.cita: Star Tales, Tucana (tucana.html, sin www): Keyser y De Houtman; Plancius (1598) la llamo Toucan; De Houtman (1603) describia «not a toucan but the Oriental pied hornbill»; el tucan es sudamericano: «This suggests that the original inventor of Tucana might have been Keyser», «who had visited South America before his voyage to the East Indies»; 47 Tucanae, «rated the second-best such object in the entire sky»; «Behind its tail lies Nubecula Minor, the Small Magellanic Cloud»; el 47 viene del catalogo de Bode: «Lacaille gave it no identifying number».

UMa.cita: Star Tales, Ursa Major: Ptolomeo; Calisto, compañera de Artemis, «despite Callisto's struggles», Zeus «had his way with her», convertida en osa: «For 15 years Callisto roamed the woods in the shape of a bear, but still with a human mind»; Zeus hizo a Calisto la Osa Mayor «and Arcas into Boötes»; Hera consulto a Tetis y Oceano y los «persuaded them never to let the bear bathe in the northern waters»; «Hence, as seen from mid-northern latitudes, the bear never sets below the horizon»; la broma de Thomas Hood: «the tails had become stretched when Zeus pulled the bears up into heaven». Lo de Tenerife sale del catalogo (latitud 28,3): Merak, Phecda, Alioth, Mizar y Alkaid si se ponen; la parte 14a lo comprueba.

UMi.cita: Star Tales, Ursa Minor: Tales de Mileto, segun Calimaco, «measured out the little stars of the Wain»; «the Phoenicians navigated by reference to Ursa Minor rather than Ursa Major»; Arato, Kynosoura, «dog's tail»: «This is the origin of the English word cynosure, meaning 'guiding star'»; la Polar, «Currently it lies within 1° of the exact north celestial pole», mas cerca «around AD 2100»; «In Ptolemy's day (2nd century AD) there was no bright star near the north celestial pole»; Yildun, «a mis-spelling of the Turkish word yildiz meaning 'star'».

Vel.cita: Star Tales, Vela: Lacaille dividio Argo Navis («Voilure du Navire», 1756; Vela, 1763); «Vela's brightest star is Gamma Velorum, a double star of combined magnitude 1.7»; δ y κ Velorum con ε e ι Carinae «form a cruciform shape known as the False Cross», «sometimes mistaken for the true Southern Cross, although it is larger and fainter than the real thing»; «Vela possesses no stars labelled Alpha or Beta, since these letters were allocated to the two brightest stars in Carina»; «For fainter stars in each constellation Lacaille turned to Roman letters».

Vir.cita: Star Tales, Virgo: Ptolomeo; Dike, diosa de la justicia: «Dike was supposed to have lived on Earth in the Golden Age of mankind»; cuando los hombres empeoraron se retiro a las montañas y al final «flew up to heaven, where she sits to this day next to the constellation of Libra, which some see as the scales of justice»; «Virgo is the second-largest constellation in the sky, exceeded only by the much fainter Hydra»; Spica, «a Latin name meaning 'ear of grain'»; Vindemiatrix, «grape-gatherer»; «Virgo, incidentally, contains the autumnal equinox», que «crossed the modern constellation boundary from Libra into Virgo around 730 BC».

Vol.cita: Star Tales, Volans (volans.html, sin www): Keyser y De Houtman; Plancius (1598); Bayer (1603) la llamo Piscis Volans; «In the sky the flying fish is imagined being chased by the predatory Dorado, as happens in reality»; «Sometimes the fish landed on the decks of ships and were used for food»; «The brightest stars of Volans are of only fourth magnitude, and there are no legends associated with it»; «In 1844 the English astronomer John Herschel proposed shortening it to just Volans».

Vul.significado_en: little fox (originally, 'little fox with the goose')
Vul.cita: Star Tales, Vulpecula (vulpecula.html, sin www): Hevelius (1687); en su atlas de 1690, «Vulpecula cum Ansere», la zorra con el ganso; Hevelius «explained that the fox was taking the goose to Cerberus for a shared breakfast»; «Since then the goose has flown (or been eaten), leaving just the fox»; «Its brightest star is Alpha Vulpeculae, magnitude 4.4, which lay on the fox's nose»; «In 2017 this star was officially named Anser by the International Astronomical Union»; en el borde con la Flecha, «Brocchi's Cluster, or more popularly the Coathanger».
